sunburst.name: Sunburst
sunburst.journal: A pear-shaped sun jelly. It follows open Sunpetals the way heat follows a cleared bed.

ribbon.name: Ribbon
ribbon.hint: A dry lawn is keeping something long and bright away.
ribbon.journal: A long brook jelly. The wild water beyond the hedge is not its home. It wants a pond you keep.

berrybunch.name: Berrybunch
berrybunch.hint: Sweet crops may be drawing a crowd.
berrybunch.journal: Stacked berry jellies. They show up when Petal Corn is ripe and the stall is a real place.

rendle.name: Rendle
rendle.hint: Where a sun jelly settles, a flatter appetite follows.
rendle.journal: A low, wide jelly that follows Sunbursts. What it leaves in the soil is useful. What it takes off the stalk is not.

coriark.name: Coriark
coriark.hint: After dark, if the soil turns strange.
coriark.journal: A tall dusk jelly. Nightbloom and a dim hour bring it out of the hedges.

ruffles.name: Ruffles
ruffles.hint: A lantern in a lived-in garden.
ruffles.journal: A ruffled botanical jelly. It nests where a habitat lantern is actually hanging.

cradling.name: Cradling
cradling.hint: A garden that has been loved in daylight.
cradling.journal: A crown jelly that treats a flower-heavy garden as a nursery. It wants benches, not a spectacle.

pegacorn.name: Pegacorn
pegacorn.hint: A rare clear day, and a garden already full.
pegacorn.journal: A crested jelly with a botanical sail. No hooves, no horned horse. It crosses the hedge only when the grove is already somebody's home.

cushion.name: Cushion
cushion.hint: The sound of a stall that is actually open.
cushion.journal: A squat shop jelly. It dozes by the counter once the garden has a resident and the till has rung.
